source_candidate.candidate: SGM long-run statistical gate implementation audit

paper.title: SGM: A Statistical Godel Machine for Risk-Controlled Recursive Self-Modification

findings.paper_contract: The manuscript's one-sided empirical-Bernstein lower bound is mu_hat - sqrt(2*sigma_hat^2*ln(3/delta)/n) - 3*(b-a)*ln(3/delta)/n.
findings.public_long_driver: eb_lower_bound computes the variance term but comments out the additive bounded-range term and returns mu-term1.
findings.cross_check: A sibling public implementation, PGM_Ex6/outer_in100.py, includes term2 and returns mu-term1-term2.
findings.implication: The manuscript's empirical-Bernstein/PAC guarantee cannot be attached to the current public long-driver acceptance rule as written.

findings.scope: This is a mathematical counterexample to a distribution-free nominal-delta interpretation of the current truncated bound; it is not a claim about the realized ImageNet trajectory.

findings.paper_contract: The manuscript defines bounded normalized observations linearly as Delta/R.
findings.public_long_driver: Confirmation uses tanh((proposal-incumbent)/rmax_pp) before the lower bound.
findings.implication: A certificate for positive mean transformed utility is not by itself a certificate for positive raw expected improvement. A transformed utility can be valid if explicitly chosen, but the protected estimand must be stated accordingly.

findings.paper_contract: The supervised-learning protocol states that screening and confirmation use disjoint seed pools.
findings.public_long_launcher: run_long.sh supplies screening seeds 41,42,43 and confirm_n_seeds=12.
findings.public_long_driver: make_seed_set returns the base screening seeds plus additional seeds, so confirmation reuses 41,42,43.
findings.implication: The current long path departs from the paper's stated disjoint screening/confirmation protocol independently of the bound-formula mismatch.

findings.public_long_driver: For policy=sgm, decision is ACCEPT iff lb_conf>0; harmful_accept is defined as (lb_conf<=0) and (decision==ACCEPT).
findings.implication: This flag cannot detect a truly harmful accepted edit; it only detects an impossible internal decision inconsistency under the SGM branch.

observations: README claims a 40-iteration 23.2% to 28.2% trajectory, two acceptances, about 16% of naive-confirmation compute, and cumulative risk below delta=0.1.
README points to PGM_Ex7, but current repository root has no PGM_Ex7 directory; the visible long driver is under PGM_ImageNet100.
Repository search for long_sgm.db returns only the launcher reference; no tracked long_sgm.db/proposal ledger was found.
Repository search for 28.2 and PGM_Ex7 resolves only to README text.
The current long-driver path has one visible commit and no later path commit correcting the inspected formula.
findings.scope: Absence from the current tracked public tree is not proof that private/untracked run artifacts never existed. The reported numerical trajectory is therefore not declared false; its exact run/code binding remains unverified.

range_term_scale_note.scope: The manuscript writes the term using full range b-a, while the code helper names its argument R; these two constants must not be conflated. Either interpretation is materially nonzero at n=12.

nonclaims: No claim that the README's 23.2% to 28.2% numerical trajectory is false.
No claim that the inspected current public file is exactly the file used for an untracked historical run beyond the path history evidence stated above.
No claim that all SGM experiments, all acceptance modes, or the SGM framework are invalid.
No claim of intent or misconduct by the authors.
The finding is limited to theorem-contract/protocol compatibility of the inspected public long-run path and the exact mathematical counterexamples stated here.
downstream_use: Treat the current public 40-proposal long driver as implementation evidence without the manuscript's empirical-Bernstein/PAC certificate. Require exact run artifact/code revision and theorem-contract audit before attaching cumulative-risk guarantees to the README long-horizon result.
